learn.title: Equal sides, equal angles
learn.body: In an isosceles triangle the two equal sides are the legs, the third side is the base, and the angles at the base are the base angles. The key fact: the base angles are equal.

learn.title: The base angles theorem
learn.body: If two sides of a triangle are equal, the angles opposite them are equal. The reverse is also true: if two angles are equal, the sides opposite them are equal. An equilateral triangle has three equal sides, so all three angles are equal, each $60^\circ$.

learn.title: Find the angles
learn.body: An isosceles triangle has apex angle $40^\circ$ at the top.
steps: The two base angles are equal, call each $b$.
$b=70$, so the base angles are $70^\circ$ each.
If a base angle is $50^\circ$ instead, the apex is $180-100=80^\circ$.

learn.title: Find a side
learn.body: The legs of an isosceles triangle are $2x+1$ and $11$.
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is $180\div3=60^\circ$. If a triangle has three $60^\circ$ angles, it is equilateral.

questions.prompt: An isosceles triangle has apex angle $40^\circ$. How large is each base angle in degrees?
An isosceles triangle has base angles of $50^\circ$. Find the apex angle in degrees.
How large is each angle of an equilateral triangle?
questions.explanation: Three equal angles that add to $180^\circ$ give $60^\circ$ each.

questions.prompt: In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are \_\_.
An isosceles triangle has legs $2x+1$ and $11$. Find $x$.
A triangle has angles $70^\circ,70^\circ,40^\circ$. How is it classified by sides?
questions.explanation: Two equal angles mean two equal sides, so it is isosceles.

questions.prompt: An equilateral triangle has perimeter 36. How long is each side?
